name: DeviceGridScene
description: A grid of devices (keyboard, mouse, TV, router, phone, server, ...) that pop in; each can be off/on/active/error and change state at given frames.

name: Device3DScene
description: Realistic 3D devices (mouse, keyboard, TV, router, phone, server, bulb, car, ... any of 65 kinds) on a turntable with labels; states off/on/active/error, state changes at frames, and an optional mouse pointer that moves and clicks.

name: ExplainScene
description: Teaching card: heading and body text revealed word by word with **bold**, ==highlight==, __underline__ and ((circle)) marks; optional staggered points, a count-up stat, a device icon and drawn arrows.

name: ConnectionScene
description: Devices (any of 65 kinds, 2D icons or realistic 3D) joined by animated links: packets, electric current, fibre light, binary bits or wireless waves. Link labels, device state changes at frames. Good for "how data/current travels from A to B".

name: CircuitScene
description: Electric circuit: battery → switch → bulb (any devices) with current flowing along copper wires; the switch and bulb turn on at frames. 2D or 3D.

caption.default: Current flows from the battery, through the switch, to the bulb.

example.title: A simple circuit
example.caption: Current flows from the battery, through the switch, to the bulb.

name: WirelessScene
description: Wireless link: router → phone (any devices) with radio waves travelling between them. 2D or 3D.

caption.default: No cable: the router sends radio waves the phone can pick up.

example.title: Wireless: data on radio waves
example.caption: No cable: the router sends radio waves the phone can pick up.

name: BlankScene
description: Empty canvas with an optional title and caption: a base for overlays (terminal, chat, notification, toggle, lock/encrypt, field lines, sound wave, progress bar, callouts, …).

name: DeviceDemoScene
description: How-to demo: an app window with an optional text field (typed, or masked like a password) and a button; a mouse pointer clicks the field, types, presses the button, and a 2D or 3D device changes state (e.g. TV off → on) with a ✓ status line.

name: BubbleSortScene
description: Visualizes bubble sort as numbered vertical bars, highlighting each comparison and animating adjacent swaps. Use it to introduce passes, comparisons, and the final sorted result.
